seo.title: Gemini CLI vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source terminal agent; free and AI Pro access moved to Antigravity in June 2026. Compare features, pricing and fit.

summary: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini models; HagiCode is a workbench that can run it as an executor. Google moved individual and free users to Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026, so check which route you can still sign in with.

content: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source (Apache 2.0) terminal agent for Gemini models. HagiCode is a desktop and web workbench that runs `gemini` as one of its Agent CLIs, adding parallel sessions, proposals and commits around it. It does not replace Gemini CLI and it does not provide Gemini access.

One thing to check first: Google says Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI for free Code Assist for individuals and for Google AI Pro and Ultra users on June 18, 2026. Gemini CLI remains available through paid Gemini or Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API keys and Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licences. HagiCode needs a `gemini` install you can still authenticate; its list of Agent CLIs does not include Antigravity CLI.
If you only want a terminal agent and your Gemini route still works, stay with Gemini CLI alone.

sections.title: Gemini CLI vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Open-source terminal AI agent from Google for Gemini models
Desktop and web AI programming workbench that drives Agent CLIs you install
Interface and platforms
Terminal UI; install via npm, Homebrew or MacPorts; headless mode with JSON output
Desktop app for Windows, macOS, Linux; Docker Compose container; Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
Apache 2.0 licence; model use needs a paid Gemini API key, Vertex/Enterprise Agent Platform, or a Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licence
Desktop and Container free; Store edition free with optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Gemini models only; Google says it is not optimised for its newest model and points to Antigravity for it
Hosts no models; uses whatever `gemini` is signed in with, so cost stays with Google
Parallel work
One session per terminal; subagents inside a session
Several concurrent sessions across repos, managed from an Agents view
Spec and planning workflow
Plan mode, todo-based task planning, checkpointing and rewind
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive; 3 concurrent on free editions, 32 with TurboEngine
Git and commit handling
Runs shell and Git commands inside the session; no dedicated commit workflow
AI-composed commits, Git management, GitHub integration, embedded Code Server editor
Setup effort
`npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` plus Google or API-key sign-in
Install HagiCode Desktop, with a working, signed-in `gemini` already on the machine
Best for
Open-source-minded developers on a paid Gemini or Code Assist route who want a terminal agent
Developers running several tasks or repos who want a GUI and a spec discipline

items.title: Open source and scriptable
content: The code is Apache 2.0 and public, which matters if you want to read how an agent handles your files or fork it. Headless mode prints text, JSON or streaming JSON, so it slots into scripts and pipelines in a way a GUI cannot.

items.title: Project memory you control
content: `GEMINI.md` context files carry project rules into every session, `.geminiignore` keeps files out, and checkpointing with rewind lets you save and resume conversations. These are plain files you can commit, which suits teams that want agent behaviour reviewed like code.

items.title: Wide feature surface in the terminal
content: Beyond editing and shell commands it offers Agent Skills, subagents, plan mode, hooks, extensions, web search and fetch, MCP servers and IDE integration. Release channels (preview, stable and nightly, published weekly or daily) let you choose how fast to move.

items.title: Several authentication routes
content: You can sign in with a Google account, use a `GEMINI_API_KEY` for usage-based billing, or use Vertex AI for enterprise setups. Sandboxing and trusted folders limit what the agent can touch. The caveat is that availability now depends on which route you use, as explained above.

sections.title: When to choose Gemini CLI, and when to choose HagiCode

items: You are on a paid Gemini API key, Vertex AI or a Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence and want a plain terminal agent.
You value the open-source Apache 2.0 code and want to fork or audit your agent.
You rely on `GEMINI.md`, hooks and extensions and want them to run in the same terminal you already use.
You need headless runs with JSON output in scripts or CI.
You work on one task at a time and do not want another application.
You run several Gemini CLI tasks across repositories and want to see their sessions side by side.
You want an OpenSpec proposal, validation and archive step before the agent edits code.
You prefer reviewing tool calls and diffs in a GUI, with AI-composed commits and an embedded Code Server.
You want Vault notes and Monospecs to carry context between your Gemini CLI sessions.
You use several Agent CLIs and want a single workspace to switch between them.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool
content: If your free Code Assist or Google AI Pro/Ultra route to Gemini CLI ended on June 18, 2026, HagiCode cannot bring it back: it needs a `gemini` CLI you can still sign in to.
Headless CI and scripted one-shot runs: call `gemini` directly.
You only want a terminal, or a quick question in an editor you already use.
Teams that do not want proposal and spec discipline; free editions also cap concurrent proposals at 3.
It adds setup compared with Gemini CLI alone and is not an IDE replacement beyond its embedded Code Server.

sections.title: Using Gemini CLI together with HagiCode

content: HagiCode starts the `gemini` executable you already installed, in its ACP mode (`--acp`), and shows the session in its own interface. Your install, authentication and Google billing stay exactly as they were.
Nothing is locked in: your repositories stay ordinary Git repositories and you can run `gemini` in a terminal at any time.

items: 1. Install Gemini CLI (`npm install -g @google/gemini-cli` or `brew install gemini-cli`) and sign in with a route that is still supported, such as an API key.
2. Install HagiCode Desktop (free) for Windows, macOS or Linux.
3. In HagiCode, choose Gemini as the Agent CLI for a session.
4. Open a repository and start a session or an OpenSpec proposal.
5. Expect Gemini models and Google billing as before; HagiCode adds workflow around them.
6. To return to plain Gemini CLI, open a terminal in the same repository and run `gemini`.

blocks.title: What works for Gemini CLI inside HagiCode
content: Works: parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals, AI commits, Code Server, Vault, Monospecs and the unified tool-call view with Gemini CLI.
Does not apply to Gemini: interactive questions (Claude, Pi, OMP and Reasonix only) and the agent work panel (Claude only).
Antigravity CLI is a different product; HagiCode's Gemini integration targets the `gemini` executable only.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Gemini CLI runs one conversation per terminal. HagiCode can keep several Gemini sessions going across repositories and show them in one Agents view.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: Your `GEMINI.md` carries rules, but not the reasoning behind a change. An OpenSpec proposal records it, is validated before the agent applies it, and is archived afterwards.

items.title: AI commits and Code Server
content: HagiCode can compose a commit message from what Gemini changed, and the embedded Code Server lets you review the edits without opening another editor.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs lets a Gemini session work across several repositories; Vault stores cross-project notes that outlast any session or context window.

items.title: One tool-call view and optional TokenMonitor
content: Gemini's tool calls appear in the same layout as every other agent, and an optional TokenMonitor can show usage in the status bar. Model access and billing remain Google's.

items: Gemini CLI is a well-equipped open-source terminal agent, but check that your sign-in route survived the June 18, 2026 change.
HagiCode is a workbench layer that runs `gemini` underneath; it adds sessions, proposals and commits, not models.
Stay with Gemini CLI alone for one-terminal and scripted work; add HagiCode for parallel, spec-driven work.

faq.question: Is Gemini CLI free?
faq.answer: The tool is open source under Apache 2.0, but model use is not free for everyone. Google says Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI for free Code Assist for individuals and for Google AI Pro and Ultra users on June 18, 2026, while paid API keys and Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licences continue.

faq.question: Is Gemini CLI discontinued?
faq.answer: Not entirely. Google moved individual users (free Code Assist, Google AI Pro and Ultra) to Antigravity CLI, but says Gemini CLI remains available through paid Gemini and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API keys, and unchanged for enterprise licences.

faq.question: How do I install Gemini CLI?
faq.answer: Run `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli`, `brew install gemini-cli`, or try it with `npx @google/gemini-cli`. Then start `gemini` and choose an authentication method.

faq.question: Can I use Gemini CLI with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes, if you have a `gemini` install that can still authenticate. Pick Gemini as the Agent CLI in HagiCode; HagiCode does not include Antigravity CLI.

faq.question: Gemini CLI vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Use Gemini CLI alone for a simple terminal agent. Add HagiCode for parallel sessions, OpenSpec proposals and a GUI over the same CLI.
